Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of Cisplatin vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which Cisplatin may alter cancer related pathways.

Introduction/Context  
We analyzed differential expression in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines treated with cisplatin versus DMSO (vehicle), using RNA-seq and DESeq2. The provided dataset (“ijms-24-14743-v2_crc_cells_cisplatin_vs_dmso_DEG.csv”) contains 20 130 genes with baseMean, log2FC, p-value, and adjusted p-value (padj). Replicate number and cell‐line identity are not specified. Using a nominal p<0.05 cutoff, 2 898 genes were deemed significant (up and down combined) and subjected to overrepresentation analysis (ORA) against the Reactome database.

Keywords  
• cisplatin • TP53/p53 signaling • cell cycle arrest • unfolded protein response • apoptosis

Candidate Genes  
TP53; CDKN1A (p21); BAX; BBC3 (PUMA); GADD45A; XBP1; DDIT3 (CHOP); HSPA5 (BiP)

Pathway Overrepresentation (Reactome_Pathways_2024) – Top Enriched Terms  

| Pathway                                              | Overlap | Adj P-value     | Genes (selected)                            |
|------------------------------------------------------|---------|-----------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Transcriptional Regulation by TP53                   | 95/362  | 7.97 × 10⁻⁸     | CDKN1A; CDKN1B; BAX; BBC3; GADD45A; MDM2; … |
| TP53 Regulates Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes     | 27/49   | 1.85 × 10⁻⁸     | CDKN1A; CDKN1B; PCNA; BAX; GADD45A; CCNE1; … |
| Unfolded Protein Response (UPR)                      | 34/95   | 7.38 × 10⁻⁶     | XBP1; DDIT3; HSPA5; ATF4; ATF6; CALR; …     |
| Loss of MECP2 Binding Ability to the NCoR SMRT Complex | 6/7    | 2.27 × 10⁻³     | MECP2; NCOR1; NCOR2; HDAC3; TBL1XR1; TBL1X   |
| Laminin Interactions                                 | 14/30   | 9.19 × 10⁻⁴     | LAMA2; LAMA3; LAMA4; ITGA2; ITGB4; COL4A5; … |

Discussion  
1. p53-Centered DNA Damage Response: The strongest enrichment is in “Transcriptional Regulation by TP53” and “TP53 Regulates Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes” (Adj P < 10⁻⁷). Key effectors CDKN1A (↑), CDKN1B (↑), GADD45A (↑), BAX (↑) and BBC3/PUMA (↑) point to cisplatin-induced DNA crosslinks activating p53, driving G₁/S and G₂/M arrest and intrinsic apoptosis.  
2. Cell Cycle Checkpoints: Upregulation of cyclin‐dependent kinase inhibitors (p21, p27) and modulation of cyclins (CCNE1/2) confirm enforced checkpoint control. Aberrant RB1/E2F interactions further underscore cell‐cycle dysregulation.  
3. Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and UPR: The “Unfolded Protein Response” (Adj P ≈ 7 × 10⁻⁶) with leading genes XBP1, DDIT3/CHOP and HSPA5/BiP suggests cisplatin imposes proteotoxic stress, potentially via misfolded protein accumulation or perturbation of ER calcium homeostasis.  
4. Chromatin and ECM Remodeling: Altered MECP2–NCoR–SMRT binding implicates epigenetic reprogramming, while enrichment of “Laminin Interactions” may reflect changes in cell–matrix adhesion, migration or metastatic potential.  

Mechanistic Implications  
Cisplatin’s cytotoxicity in CRC appears to converge on DNA damage/p53 signaling (promoting arrest and apoptosis) and ER stress/UPR activation. The upregulation of pro-apoptotic BCL2 family members (BAX, PUMA) and chaperones (HSPA5) suggests a two-pronged assault: genotoxic stress plus proteostasis disruption.

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate p53 activation and downstream targets (p21, PUMA, BAX) by Western blot or qPCR.  
2. Assess ER stress markers (BiP, CHOP) to confirm UPR engagement and test chemical chaperones for rescue.  
3. Examine changes in cell‐matrix adhesion (laminin receptors) and chromatin marks (H3K27ac) to probe ECM/epigenetic remodeling.  
4. Clarify whether these pathways are uniform across different CRC cell lines (not specified).
